official.deadline_note: Fall 2027 Round 2 opened 28 September 2026 with decisions released 14 February 2027 and the Fall semester starting 29 August 2027. Spring 2027 entry was open to PhD applicants only, with a Round 1 deadline of 27 September 2026 and decisions on 8 November 2026. KAUST states the dates are tentative and may change with application volume.
official.status_note: KAUST's Admission Timeline page states 'Applications for Spring 2027 entry are now open' (PhD only) and that Fall 2027 admission is open to M.S., M.S./Ph.D. and Ph.D. applicants.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (worth up to USD $35,000 per year).
benefits: Full tuition and bench fee coverage (worth up to USD $35,000 per year)
A monthly stipend (worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students, and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students depending on qualifications and academic progress)
Base accommodation included: shared accommodation for single students, 2-bed accommodation for married students
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Relocation support covering visa, relocation and travel costs
Eligible students can request a housing upgrade, subject to an additional fee
eligibility: Bachelor's degree in a subject relevant to the programme applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Master's programmes

Master's degree in a subject relevant to the programme applied to, from a recognized higher education institution, for entry into Ph.D. programmes; Professional Master's degrees are not regarded as directly equivalent and must be declared
At least 18 years of age on entry
Minimum permitted GPA of 3.0 on a 4-point scale or equivalent (typically 90% of admitted applicants have a GPA above 3.3 and 75% above 3.5)
Evidence of proficiency in the English language
requirements: Submit an application through the KAUST online application portal before the published round deadline
Official university transcripts showing courses, credits where applicable, grades, final grade or award and the grading scale used
Curriculum Vitae and statement of purpose of approximately 750 words
Contact details of 3 referees with academic or professional email addresses; personal email addresses are not accepted
A clear, unobscured copy of the passport page showing picture and personal details (Saudi applicants may provide a national ID card)
All supporting documents, including transcripts, must be in English; if your transcript is not in English upload the original plus a certified English translation
An official English language test score if available (GRE or PGAT scores may be submitted but are not compulsory)
documents: Official university transcripts (or most recent available academic record if the degree is not yet complete)
Certified English translation of non-English transcripts
Official English language test score, if available
Clear, unobscured copy of the passport page (or national ID card for Saudi applicants)
Final official transcript sent directly by the awarding institution before arrival, if admitted
selection_criteria: Holistic review of academic achievements and personal qualities such as motivation and potential impact in the scientific community
Stage two faculty review committee evaluation and ranking against other applicants, with shortlisting for interviews
Academic interview and/or test where invited
All admission decisions are final and will not be reconsidered; KAUST cannot provide individual feedback on specific applications
coverage: Full tuition and bench fee coverage, worth up to USD $35,000 per year
Monthly stipend worth USD $20,000 per year for M.S. students and USD $25,000 to $30,000 per year for Ph.D. students
Health insurance for students and eligible dependents living on campus
Visa, relocation and travel costs for the initial move to KAUST and the return home upon graduation
application_method: Log into the KAUST application portal and submit before the round deadline
Upload transcripts, CV, statement of purpose, passport page and English test score
Enter 3 referees' contact details, which sends reference requests to them automatically
Respond to any invitation for an online interview with KAUST faculty from your subject area
Await the decision notification by email in the round's notification window
official.application_route: Single online application through the KAUST admissions portal; the Fellowship is awarded automatically to admitted students and there is no separate funding application.
official.study_mode: Full-time, on campus at KAUST, Thuwal
official.international_eligibility: KAUST is a community of over 120 nationalities and applicants of any nationality may apply; those requiring a visa are supported through the Fellowship's relocation support.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Research must be within KAUST's programmes of study; the degree held must be relevant to the programme applied to.
official.research_requirement: A statement of purpose of approximately 750 words covering past work, preparation for the intended field, background and interests, academic plans and career objectives.
official.duration: M.S. is a 36-credit programme expected to be completed in three semesters and one summer session; the M.S./Ph.D. pathway typically takes five to six years
official.description: The KAUST Fellowship is designed so that admitted graduate students can focus entirely on their studies and research with the peace of mind that comes from financial support. KAUST calculates the total value of the Fellowship at between $70k and $80k per year depending on the student's specific situation.
official.english_requirement: IELTS 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in all individual sections (IELTS Online accepted); TOEFL iBT 5.0 overall with at least 4.5 in all individual sections (KAUST Admissions code 4107, TOEFL Home Edition accepted); PTE Academic 71 overall with at least 67 in all individual sections; or Cambridge C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency 185 overall with at least 176 in all individual sections. Scores are valid for two years from the test date. Not accepted as evidence: Medium of Instruction certificates, the Duolingo English Test (except for Visiting Student applicants), TOEFL MyBest superscores, and IELTS One Skill Retake results.

not_confirmed: exact stipend value for an individual student (published only as ranges)
tuition_coverage amount beyond the stated up-to-USD $35,000 annual figure
verification.notes: All figures read directly on KAUST's own admissions domain. funding_amount is recorded as 70000, the lower bound of the published statement that 'the value of the KAUST Fellowship is calculated to be worth between $70k and $80k per year'; the component figures (tuition/bench fees up to USD 35,000 per year; stipend USD 20,000 per year M.S. and USD 25,000-30,000 per year Ph.D.) are carried verbatim in benefits and coverage. Deadline dates confirmed on the Admission Timeline page.

applicant_utility.summary: The KAUST Fellowship is automatic once you are admitted, so the only application that matters is the admissions application and it closes on 3 January 2027 for Fall 2027 Round 2 with decisions on 14 February 2027. Build the file around a 750-word statement of purpose and three referees with institutional email addresses, because KAUST rejects personal email addresses and expects references within seven calendar days of the deadline. Secure a valid IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL 5.0 / PTE 71 / Cambridge 185 score, or qualify for the in-person degree exemption from the US, Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia or New Zealand, since Medium of Instruction certificates and the Duolingo test are not accepted.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong science, engineering and mathematics graduates with a relevant degree, a GPA comfortably above 3.0 and a clearly articulated research direction.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your three referees before entering their details, since reference requests fire immediately and late references delay the application
Book an English test early enough that the score date is within two years at the time you apply
Chase a complete transcript that shows the grading scale, not just grades
Declare any Professional Master's degree explicitly if you are applying for a Ph.D.
Scan the passport page unobscured, with picture and personal details readable
Plan finances for a housing upgrade if you want one, since base accommodation is shared for single students
common_rejection_risks: Referees submitting after the seven-day window, which stalls the whole application
Submitting a Medium of Instruction certificate, a Duolingo score, a TOEFL MyBest superscore or an IELTS One Skill Retake, all of which KAUST will not accept
GPA near the 3.0 floor, when 90% of admitted applicants sit above 3.3
A statement of purpose that reads as generic rather than tied to a KAUST programme and faculty
Assuming a GRE score will compensate for weak academics, since KAUST is explicit that admission decisions are final and no feedback is given
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any housing upgrade fee, and costs for dependents or family members not covered as eligible dependents living on campus; relocation support covers only the initial move and the return home on graduation.
document_audit: A non-English transcript needs both the original and a certified translation uploaded together
If your degree is not finished you may submit a partial or unofficial transcript, but an official final transcript must come directly from the awarding institution before arrival
Saudi applicants should use a national ID card rather than a passport
alerts: Students with external sponsorship or funding may not be eligible for the KAUST Fellowship
You can submit without an English score, but you must meet the minimum before enrolment and a competitive applicant should include it
Saudi nationals and Ph.D. students with IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 4.5 / PTE 64 / Cambridge 176 may be admitted on condition of taking the Academic English Language Communication Course in the first year
There is a limited time to respond to an offer or the decision may be withdrawn
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online portal submission, document review, faculty ranking and shortlisting, online interview if invited, then an emailed decision within the round's notification window.
